A particle starts at the point with position vector (2i + 5j) m and moves with constant velocity (3i − 4j) m s⁻¹. (a) Find the speed of the particle. (b) Write down its position vector t seconds after it starts. (c) Find the time at which the i-component of its position vector is 14 and its distance from the origin at that time.

At noon, ship P is at the origin and moves with constant velocity (4i + 3j) km h⁻¹. At the same time, ship Q is at the point with position vector (24i − 6j) km and moves with constant velocity (−4i + aj) km h⁻¹. The two ships meet. Find the time at which they meet, the value of a and the position vector of the meeting point.
scheme: M1: position vectors at time t: P = 4ti + 3tj and Q = (24 − 4t)i + (−6 + at)j
A1: t = 3, so they meet at 15:00

questions.q: What is the derivative of f(x) = e^(3x) with respect to x?
questions.why: By the chain rule, d/dx[e^(kx)] = k e^(kx). For k = 3, the derivative is 3e^(3x).

(a) Find the values of t when the particle is at rest. (b) Find the acceleration at the second of these times. (c) Find the total distance travelled in the first 4 seconds.
scheme: A1: v = 0 at t = 1 and t = 4
A1: a = 18 m s⁻² at t = 4
M1: s(1) = 11 and s(4) = −16, so the particle changes direction at t = 1
